newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Bhutto dismissal seems constitutional.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Bhutto dismissal seems constitutional.

text.p: The United States said the dismissal of Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto on Tuesday appeared to be constitutional.
"The dismissal of the government appears to be in accordance with the Pakistani constitution," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Burns said the United States had had longstanding "good relations" with Pakistan and expected to continue them with the interim government and whatever government was elected in polls set for February.
The United States had no advance warning from Pakistan of Bhutto's dismissal, Burns said.
Bhutto was fired on Tuesday for the second time in her turbulent political career by Pakistan's president, who accused her government of corruption, nepotism and misrule.
"Obviously we have an interest in stability in Pakistan," Burns said, adding: "We will try to accentuate the positive in our relations with Pakistan."
He stressed the importance of Pakistan sticking with constitutional processes.

Burns acknowledged the transition would make it harder to cooperate on regional issues. "But we'll have to make do as best we can in working with the interim government, certainly on Afghanistan, which is a pertinent issue right now."
